- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.33) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; apply downward bias correction, especially in early forecast horizon.
- When sentiment is negative (≤-0.33), model often underestimates; apply upward bias correction, particularly for short-term (1-7 day) forecasts.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 5.0), model frequently overcorrects with exaggerated declines; cap subsequent forecast drops at 30% of peak or adjust downward by 1.5x the sentiment magnitude.
- If sentiment history shows repeated volatility (alternating +/–), model exhibits mean-reversion bias; smooth forecasts toward recent 7-day average, especially for mid-term (8-20 day) horizon.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often fails to capture long-term mean reversion; apply exponential decay weighting toward recent 10-day average to reduce overconfidence in distant outcomes.
- When sentiment is flat (0.00) for 3+ consecutive days, model tends to drift toward historical mean; adjust forecast by subtracting 0.1–0.3x the historical 30-day average if no recent volatility.
